bullets.title: META: Bullish AI monetization narrative drives ~10% rally; KeyBanc raises PT to $790
bullets.body: META surged ~10% on Muse Spark 1.1 (agentic reasoning at ~25% cost of rivals, priced at $1.25/$4.25/M tokens), plans to double compute to 14GW by 2027 (~$210B capex), and an Iris in-house AI chip entering production in September. KeyBanc raises PT to $790 (OW), introducing 2028E revenue of $366.9B and EPS of $39.49; bull case $1,065 at 25x. EU DSA finding (addictive design, potential 6% revenue fine) and $1.4T teen mental health penalty risk are key bear offsets. Tencent leading deal to unwind Meta's $2B Manus acquisition per China regulator order.

bullets.title: NVDA: NDR reaffirms accelerating, diversified growth; memory shortage seen persisting years
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reiterates Overweight/Top Pick following NVDA NDR; management described three growth segments (AI labs 20%, hyperscalers 50%, neoclouds/enterprise/sovereign ~50% of DC) and $20B CPU target. NVDA noted compute costs for its own AI team now exceed employee salaries. Memory shortage expected to persist for several years per NVDA's demand visibility. NVDA -0.4-0.6% pre-market in mixed Mag-7 session.

bullets.title: MU: Raises US investment to $250B through 2035; poured first NY fab concrete; 2026 profit seen eclipsing prior 35 years
bullets.body: Micron increased FY2026E net capex to $27B+ and anticipates FY2027E capex of $45B+, raising total US planned investment to >$250B through 2035. Construction milestone: first concrete poured at Clay, NY fab. HBM prices could more than double in 2027 per Jefferies; memory prices up ~4x in current cycle with potential 2-3x further upside before 85%+ margin ceiling is hit.

bullets.title: NFLX: 2Q preview; JPM OW at $118; engagement concerns cloud narrative ahead of July 16 earnings
bullets.body: JPM maintains Overweight with $118 PT; models 2Q revenue $12.58B (+12% FXN Y/Y) and 31.7% OI margin. Global DAU down -6% Y/Y vs +8% subscriber growth; TV viewership share fell to 7.8% in April 2026 (lowest since May 2025). NFLX exploring live TV channels and Peacock bundle to boost engagement; 'Cancel Netflix' search queries spiked post-price hike but normalized. Stock down ~22% since start of 2Q. Consensus EPS $0.79, revenue $12.58B for July 16 report.

bullets.title: STX: Wells Fargo upgrades to Overweight, raises PT to $1,100 from $900; reports July 16
bullets.body: Wells Fargo (Aaron Rakers) upgrades Seagate Technology to Overweight, raising PT to $1,100 from $900 (24% upside) ahead of July 16 earnings (consensus EPS $5.09, revenue $3.49B). GS TMT also flags upgrade in sector roundup. AI-driven HDD demand and data center storage cycle underpins thesis.

bullets.title: SHOP: Stifel upgrades to Buy, raises PT to $150 from $110; UBS hosting Payments partnership expert call
bullets.body: Stifel upgrades Shopify from Hold to Buy, raising PT to $150 from $110 (+22% upside from $123). Stock up ~2.5% pre-market. UBS also hosting expert call July 17 on Shopify Payments partnership ecosystem and Adyen competitive dynamics.

bullets.title: FOXA: Rothschild upgrades to Buy, PT $71 (+32%) on Roku deal upside
bullets.body: Rothschild & Co Redburn upgrades Fox Corp to Buy from Neutral, raising PT to $71 from $48 (32% upside), citing valuation and upside from Roku deal. FactSet consensus target $71.53. Stock +1.4% pre-market.

bullets.title: Semis pre-market: INTC/MU/SNDK/WDC/MRVL/TXN/LITE under pressure; TSMC CoWoS raised
bullets.body: Semiconductor sector broadly weak pre-market: INTC -2.4%, SNDK -2.6%, MU -1.6%, WDC -1.8%, LITE -1.4%, TXN -1.3%, MRVL -1.3%. JPM raises TSMC FY26/27/28 CoWoS capacity estimates by 1%/9%/11% to 115k/190k/225k wfpm; demand-supply gap for advanced packaging widened to ~20% on agentic AI CPU demand. Taiwan H1 2026 semi exports +43.9% YoY to $133.17B; DRAM exports +158.5%.

bullets.title: GOOGL: KeyBanc raises PT to $445; Cloud projected at $102B in 2026E; ad spend +7.1% Y/Y in 2Q
bullets.body: KeyBanc raises GOOGL PT to $445 (from prior), introducing 2028E revenue of $724.4B and EPS of $17.80. Google Cloud revenue forecast $23.4B in 2Q (+72% Y/Y); total backlog expected to surpass $480B. Citi ad survey shows Google ad spend +7.1% Y/Y in 2Q, projected +7.4% in 3Q; Search CTRs +2.65% Y/Y. Piper flags positive technical signals, back above 50-day MA.

bullets.title: Online advertising: 2Q spend +8.4% Y/Y, beats expectations; META and RDDT top picks
bullets.body: Citi's Inventus Media tracker shows 2Q ad spend +8.4% Y/Y, ~90bps above forecast; World Cup contributed ~200bps. 3Q projected at +7.8% Y/Y. Piper's Internet Wave 1 preview rates META as top large-cap pick and RDDT as top SMID (up 43% since 2Q start). APP gaining most supply share in mobile gaming with top ROAS; mobile gaming ad spend growth +9% Y/Y.

bullets.title: CRM: KeyBanc downgrades to Sector Weight on valuation; AI monetization not yet visible
bullets.body: KeyBanc downgrades Salesforce from Overweight to Sector Weight; CRM trades at 3.8x CY26 EV/revenue vs. sector avg 5.3x and is fairly valued at 21x CY27 P/E. Agentforce AI monetization anecdotally building but not confirmed in model; CIO survey shows shift toward security/hardware over application projects. NOW customers pulling forward renewals ahead of July 1 SKU pricing changes.

bullets.title: DIS: Exploring free-tier Disney+ content; streaming engagement battle intensifies
bullets.body: Disney is discussing enabling free-tier content on Disney+ to compete with YouTube for TV viewers, per Business Insider. Combined with NFLX exploring live TV and bundles, the streaming sector is pivoting toward engagement-preservation strategies. DIS+/Hulu bundle costs $11.99/month (with ads).

bullets.title: CYBR/PANW: DA Davidson Q2 VAR survey bullish; strongest pipeline in 4+ years
bullets.body: DA Davidson Q2 cybersecurity VAR survey shows record-high share of VARs indicating increased security software demand; average pipeline strength strongest in 4+ years. CYBR/PANW (BUY): win rates improved vs. 11 of 12 competitors post-acquisition, minimal GTM disruption. CVLT and VRNS also receive BUY ratings; TENB weakest feedback among VM vendors.

bullets.title: LITE/COHR: AI infrastructure demand broadening; photonics sector bottleneck thesis intact
bullets.body: Multiple sources highlight AI capex broadening beyond hyperscalers to neoclouds, European data centers, and sovereign compute as incremental photonics demand drivers. JPM raises Google TPU 2027 shipments +11% to 8.9M units and AWS Trainium +6% to 3.5M units, both positive for LITE and COHR. LITE flagging InP capacity expansion on recent calls as photonics shifts from optics subtopic to critical AI bottleneck. Bear case: cyclical oversupply end-game risk noted.

bullets.title: MSFT: Xbox cutting 1,600 jobs; ChatGPT 5.6 on Copilot; carbon emissions +25% YoY
bullets.body: Microsoft Xbox division cutting 1,600 jobs. ChatGPT 5.6 now available on MSFT Copilot per Wolfe SaaS note. MSFT carbon emissions rose 25% YoY despite sustainability commitments. Jefferies notes MSFT 'uninspiring despite S&P discount' in positioning survey; IGV down -14.3% YTD.

bullets.title: INTC: JPMorgan lists as top short; Intel revised 2026 capex flat with equipment +25% YoY
bullets.body: JPMorgan lists INTC among top short ideas for 3Q26 (Underweight). Citi notes Intel revised 2026E gross capex to flat YoY with equipment spending +25% YoY; potential upside from Terafab, Apple/Google foundry partnerships, and Ohio fab expansion. Twitter commentary highlights Intel's challenged position in memory hierarchy vs. peers.

bullets.title: DLR: Citi maintains Buy; 2Q bookings expected light but AI inference demand accelerating
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on Digital Realty ahead of 2Q26; models bookings $186M vs. LTM average $224M but sees favorably AI inference as incremental demand driver. FY26 revenue forecast $6.75B, Adjusted EBITDA $3.73B, both above consensus. Room for multiple expansion from positive renewal spreads and conservative organic guidance.

bullets.title: SPOT: Record labels pushing AI-generated music labeling, signals potential licensing deals
bullets.body: RIAA and IFPI proposing two AI content tags for music platforms (fully AI-generated vs. AI-assisted). Record labels (UMG, WMG, SONY) pushing Spotify to label AI-generated tracks, signaling potential AI licensing deals that could affect SPOT's content cost structure.

bullets.title: PINS: JPMorgan top short list; ad spend share gains modest vs META/APP
bullets.body: JPMorgan lists PINS among top short ideas for 3Q26 alongside INTC, WIX, IREN, and CAR. Piper's Internet preview also shows NFLX down 22% and PINS not a top pick, while META and RDDT gain share. Jefferies ad tech survey shows META +144bps and APP +169bps in e-commerce ad spend share vs. no notable PINS gains.

bullets.title: TSLA: Mixed social commentary; TSLA down 10% YTD vs Nasdaq +16%; FSD praised by users
bullets.body: TSLA trading volume reportedly near pre-Trump lows; stock down 10% YTD while Nasdaq up 16%. User reports on X praise Tesla FSD as 'magical' and at impressive capability levels. TSLA cut to junk credit status per social media report (HOG also cut to junk). No fundamental research upgrades or downgrades in the window.
